discovery: The optical lattice clock: precision timekeeping with neutral atoms trapped at the magic wavelength

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: The University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

motivation: Katori proposed (2001-2003) trapping many neutral atoms in an optical lattice tuned to a 'magic wavelength', where the light shift cancels for both clock states, so that Lamb-Dicke confinement and large atom numbers could be combined without perturbing the transition frequency. He realized the first strontium lattice clocks and later cryogenic and transportable versions. Ye, with exquisite laser stabilization and control of atomic interactions, pushed lattice clocks to 10^-18 and beyond, resolving gravitational redshift across a millimetre-scale atomic sample. These clocks, using Sr, Yb and Hg, now exceed caesium standards by two orders of magnitude, drive the redefinition of the SI second, enable relativistic geodesy, and provide sensitive tabletop searches for dark matter, variation of fundamental constants and new forces. The lattice clock is an ingenious idea that opened an entire field of precision physics with ultracold atoms.
